Nelipyno Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Zakarpatska oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. The first Jews arrived in Nelipyno in the first half of the 18th century, with 9 residents by 1830; the population grew to 209 (26.3 percent) by 1880, 300 by 1893, 496 by 1921, and 542 by 1930, engaged as tradesmen and artisans. Following the March 1939 Hungarian occupation, Jews were persecuted and forced out of their occupations; the population reached 672 by 1941, with many drafted into forced labor battalions or sent to the Eastern Front, where most perished. In August 1941, Jews without Hungarian citizenship were expelled to German-occupied Kamianets-Podilskyi and shot, and the remaining Jews of Nelipyno were deported to Auschwitz in mid-May 1944.
